writeup.p: S1DPacketEntityEffect applies one potion effect to one entity. The server has three send sites: EntityTrackerEntry broadcasts an entity's new effect to every player watching it, EntityPlayerMP.addPotionEffect and refreshActivePotionEffect send it to the affected player directly, and ServerConfigurationManager replays effects (beacon, team) on respawn and on player join. Wire layout is entityId VarInt, effectId byte, amplifier byte, duration VarInt in ticks, hideParticles boolean. In 1.8.9 the effect is a full state push: the client stores it in the entity's active potion map and the server never asks for confirmation.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleEntityEffect runs on the client thread via PacketThreadUtil, resolves the entity with getEntityByID, and for EntityLivingBase targets builds a PotionEffect(effectId, duration, amplifier, false, hideParticles), calls setPotionDurationMax(duration), then addPotionEffect. From that point every renderer (armor, HUD, particles, the player's own effect tab) reads the entity's activePotionMap. Effects on non-living entities are silently dropped, and an unknown entityId does nothing.

The 8 reference clients leave S1D to vanilla; the only non-vanilla hit among them is Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 NetworkAPI.java, which registers S1DPacketEntityEffect in the clientbound class table (index 72) so scripts can build and inject it via receivePacket. Effect-aware features in those clients (effect HUD rows, potion ESP) poll the entity's active potion map after vanilla applies the packet, or render from EntityLivingBase state, so no packet interception is needed. November Recode 2.0 is the exception: AutoPotModule hooks S1D as the server's implicit confirmation that a thrown splash potion landed, resetting its potion sequence only when the effect packet for the local player arrives. The PotionHUD/AntiPotion entries in older packet docs come from Sigma 3.9, which is not part of the reference set; Sigma 4.11's corpus has no S1D hit.

Cancelling S1D in a receive event is a client-side potion bypass: the server keeps applying the effect and its movement math, the client simply never renders or stores it. That grants nothing for movement because speed, jump and health attributes are server-authoritative. Anti-cheats never measure this packet; it is one-directional cosmetic state. The only bandwidth note is that EntityTrackerEntry sends one S1D per effect per tracked entity on the tracking loop, so rapid effect churn is amplification surface for griefing plugins, not for cheat modules.

overview: Effect application is a pure server-to-client state push. The 8 reference clients have no module interest in it and every effect-aware feature reads the entity's potion map after vanilla applies the packet; the sole non-vanilla hit among them is Rise 6.x NetworkAPI registering the class for script injection. November Recode 2.0's AutoPotModule is the only module that hooks S1D, using it as the ack that a splash potion actually applied.
server_handling: EntityTrackerEntry line 418 sends S1D to each playerNetServerHandler in the watching list when a tracked entity gains an effect; EntityPlayerMP lines 922/927 send it to the affected player for addPotionEffect and refreshActivePotionEffect; ServerConfigurationManager lines 193/509 replay active effects on respawn and join. The server does no validation on the receiving side: there is no processX handler because the packet is clientbound only.
protocol_notes: The amplifier byte is the level minus one (0 means level I). Duration is in ticks on the wire; the client stores it as the effect duration and also as durationMax, so the potion icon countdown and the expiry timestamp both come from this single value. hideParticles maps to the PotionEffect showParticles flag; an S1D with the same effectId overwrites the previous entry in the active potion map rather than stacking.
anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat in the 1.8.9 ecosystem flags S1D handling. Movement-relevant effects (speed, jump boost, slowness) are validated from server-side attribute and motion math, so a client that drops the packet only sees wrong visuals. Servers that want to detect a modified client would have to query the client for its potion state, which vanilla 1.8.9 has no packet for.

modules.name: AutoPotModule (pot confirmation)
modules.purpose: Use the S1D effect packet for the local player as the server-side confirmation that a thrown splash potion landed, so the potion sequence only advances after the effect applies.
modules.how_it_works: The potion sequence is staged: C09 held-item change, C08 block placement for the throw, then the module sets waitingClientUpdate and waits. The S1D listener checks the packet's entity id against the local player; while waitingClientUpdate is set it resets the pot stage, restarts the delay timer and re-syncs the inventory, scheduling the next pot.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None: the module only reads S1D. The effect arrives for any potion the server applies, so the ack also fires when a server-side effect lands, which only makes the sequence more robust.
modules.variations: No other client in the reference corpus hooks S1D at module level; effect-aware features elsewhere poll the active potion map instead.

general_hooks: The only module in the reference corpus registering a packet receive handler for S1D is November Recode 2.0's AutoPotModule (EventPacket.In). Rise 6.x NetworkAPI exposes clientbound packets to JavaScript scripts by class-table index.
client_variations: Memeware 7.3, Nekoware v1 private, Sigma 4.11, Spicy and Tenacity 6.0 ship the vanilla handler byte-for-byte. Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 additionally register the class in NetworkAPI (script/api/NetworkAPI.java). November Recode 2.0 is the only client that reads S1D in a module, inside AutoPotModule's EventPacket.In listener.
